title: Episodic memory snowball investigation and temporary playbook
body:
Summary:

This document captures an on-call investigation into a class of production incidents we’re calling "episodic memory snowball" events. Symptoms are sudden host-level resident memory climbs over the course of several minutes that don't correlate with a single large allocation, culminating in either host eviction or severe tail latency as the OS starts swapping. The pattern repeats in bursts across multiple hosts in a rack over 30–90 minutes.

Why this matters:
- These events caused 4 customer-facing degradations in November (elevated token latency, request timeouts) and triggered two Dedicated pool host replacements.
- They are distinct from single-point OOMs: allocation velocity is moderate but sustained, and fragmentation / page-table overhead appears amplified.

Observed signals and quick checks performed during triage:
- Per-host telemetry: resident set size (RSS) increases slowly while heap allocation rate (application-level) is relatively flat.
- /proc/<pid>/smaps shows many small anonymous mappings that grow over time.
- KV cache hit ratio steady; but kv-index shards report growing tombstone counts and reallocs.
- Prefetch worker counts spike correlated with traffic microbursts.
- dmesg showed occasional page allocation stalls and "zone_alloc_failed" messages on affected hosts.
- Traces show long tail stalls inside the C++ thread pool when a cache eviction and a prefetch try to touch the same range concurrently.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Fragmentation feedback loop: repeated small allocations from prefetch + async tokenization + per-request temporary buffers lead to heap fragmentation. Fragmentation increases allocator metadata and VM mappings (more VMA), which raises RSS and slows allocations, which in turn increases prefetch backlog and more allocations (snowball).
2) KV index churn: aggressive kv-cache metadata compaction/rehash during heavy churn causes large-ish short-lived allocations repeatedly (metadata buffers resizing) that the kernel does not coalesce quickly.
3) Prefetch concurrency spike: prefetch threads racing on eviction locks cause repeated touch/unmap cycles on the same pages (thrashing), increasing page-table churn and kernel bookkeeping.

Experiments run (summary):
- Local sim: replayed production-prefetch trace against dev hosts with varying prefetch worker counts. Observed that reducing prefetch workers by 50% eliminated sustained RSS climbs in the sim.
- Instrumented allocator: built a small build with jemalloc stats enabled; sampled VMA counts and allocation sizes during a reproducer. Confirmed VMA growth and many small allocations (~<4KB region) over time.
- KV metadata throttle: added a temporary guard to slow down rehash/compaction and observed reduced peak RSS at cost of slightly higher kv lookup latency.

Temporary mitigations (short-term playbook to run while root cause is finalized):
- If host RSS growth > 75% of host mem for 5m: restrict prefetch concurrency on that host via /api/ops/host-control (route: ops-host-throttle). Command: curl -X POST https://ops-api/hosts/<host>/controls -d '{"prefetch_workers": 2}' (this is a guarded endpoint; use oncall token).
- Apply autoscaler soft-throttle for the affected rack to avoid simultaneous replacements (prevents cascading evictions).
- Patch: deploy kv-metadata-throttle flag across canary hosts (PR: linked_artifacts[1]) to reduce rehash parallelism.
- Increase eviction hysteresis: bump kv-cache eviction thresholds by +10% for impacted pools for 24h.

Triage & runbook steps (stepwise):
1) Identify candidate hosts: query metric host_resident_bytes (last 30m) and filter for hosts with >10% sustained increase and high VMA count. Sample query (Datadog): avg(last_5m):increase(host.resident_bytes{pool:dedi} by host) > 0.10
2) Capture a heap snapshot and smaps: sudo gcore <pid> && cat /proc/<pid>/smaps > /tmp/smaps-$(date +%s).log
3) Temporarily reduce prefetch workers: POST to ops-api (see temporary mitigations). Confirm prefetch worker count drops and monitor resident bytes.
4) Enable jemalloc/procstats on the process or attach pmap to capture VMA distribution.
5) If kv metadata churn correlated (high rehash_ops/sec): enable kv-metadata-throttle toggle via feature flag for the pool.
6) If host remains above 85% mem after 10m: move tenants off host via host-drain (evict-light) to avoid abrupt OOMs. Use the host-drain tool in the ops console — keep docs for impact to SLA.

Observability checklist (what to watch):
- host.resident_bytes (per-host, 1m & 5m)
- process.vma_count or jemalloc_extents (when enabled)
- kv.rehash_ops_per_sec and kv.tombstones_per_shard
- prefetch.worker_count and prefetch.task_queue_depth
- syslog/dmesg for zone allocation failures or pfault spikes
- tail of request latency (p95/p99 token time)

Longer-term remediation candidates (owners suggested):
- Allocator strategy change: investigate switching the runtime to a different arena configuration or tune jemalloc tunables that reduce VMA fragmentation (owner: eng-serving-runtime / Priya Nambiar).
- Prefetch backpressure: implement a work-conserving backpressure token that ties prefetch concurrency to host free memory (owner: serving-runtime / Jonas Reed).
- KV metadata redesign: reduce per-shard rehash parallelism and use smaller incremental compactions (owner: storage team / Ethan Cole).
- Per-tenant soft caps: avoid heavy tenants causing host-level snowball by introducing soft allocation quotas and gradual routing away under memory pressure (owner: platform-engineering).

Simulation notes and scripts used (dev pointers):
- reproducer: infra/tools/prefetch-replay (use sample traces in traces/prefetch/2024-11-replay.tar.gz)
- jemalloc build flags used: MALLOC_CONF=background_thread:false,lg_chunk:20,lg_tcache_max:8
- sample Datadog query snippets are in the linked confluence page (linked_artifacts[2]).

Open action items (short):
- [P0] Roll kv-metadata-throttle to all Dedicated canaries and monitor (owner: Ethan; ETA: 2d).
- [P1] Add a guarded ops endpoint to reduce per-host prefetch concurrency (owner: SRE tooling; ETA: 3d).
- [P1] Add VMA/extent telemetry to the standard process-level dashboard (owner: observability; ETA: 1w).
- [P2] Prototype memory-aware prefetch backpressure algorithm in staging (owner: serving-runtime; ETA: 3w).

Notes to future oncall:
- This pattern is subtle: look for sustained VMA growth without a single large allocation. The root cause is likely simultaneous interactions (prefetch + kv metadata + allocator) rather than a single subsystem.
- When rolling temporary mitigations, do small rollouts and watch canary pools for regression in latency.

Appendix — commands and helper snippets:
- List top memory processes per host: ps aux --sort=-rss | head -n 10
- Dump smaps for process: sudo cat /proc/$(pgrep serving-runtime)/smaps > /tmp/smaps-$(date +%s).log
- Quick pmap summary: sudo pmap -x $(pgrep serving-runtime) | tail -n 10
- Reduce prefetch on host: curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ONCALL_TOKEN' https://ops-api/hosts/<host>/controls -d '{"prefetch_workers":2}'
- Host drain (soft): opsctl host drain --mode=evict-light --host <host> --reason "memory-snowball"

Acknowledgements:
Thanks to Priya for the jemalloc instrumentation, Jonas for the prefetch trace replay harness, and Ethan for the kv-metadata throttle patch.
